claims.text: The local catalog models the Chūgoku/Shikoku World Challenge Summer participation-prize source group as one row containing Lucky Stadium at source index 169.

Bulbapedia says Lucky Stadium was first awarded to participants of the Japanese World Challenge Summer tournaments held between July and August 2000, with eight variations printed, each one exclusive to a region of Japan.
Bulbapedia lists the Chūgoku/Shikoku print, featuring Gyarados, as available at Hiroshima Sun Plaza, Hiroshima on August 2, 2000.

PokeBoon identifies Lucky Stadium [Gyarados] [Chugoku] as a World Challenge Summer participation prize and gives the Gyarados/Chugoku identity; this dossier treats its title as useful identity support while relying on Bulbapedia for the Chūgoku/Shikoku regional naming and Summer event date.
Bulbapedia's Lucky Stadium gallery credits the Chūgoku/Shikoku region print to Yousuke Hirata and CR CG gangs.
PokeBoon also credits Lucky Stadium [Gyarados] [Chugoku] to CR CG gangs and Yousuke Hirata.
Bulbapedia says all World Challenge Summer Lucky Stadium prints feature regional landmarks; the Chūgoku/Shikoku print features the floating torii at Itsukushima Shrine in Hatsukaichi.

Bulbapedia separates the regional World Challenge Summer prints from the Tropical Mega Battle bilingual print, Neo Destiny English print, Intro Pack Neo print, and Pokemon Center New York print, each of which has different artwork or route.
As judged collector texture, the Chūgoku/Shikoku print matters because Gyarados and the Itsukushima torii make the regional Stadium feel like water, threshold, and tournament memory at once.

narrative.human_title: Lucky Stadium [Gyarados] [Chūgoku/Shikoku]: the gate on the water
narrative.why_it_matters: This regional print has teeth. Gyarados is already a card-collector magnet, but here it is not just the monster; it is the force moving around a place. The floating torii at Itsukushima, the Hiroshima event route, and the World Challenge Summer map all make this Lucky Stadium feel like a threshold card: water, shrine, tournament, and regional memory crossing in one object.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A seller, collector, or agent identifies a Lucky Stadium as the World Challenge Summer Chūgoku/Shikoku participation-prize print.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Do not identify this row from Lucky Stadium or Gyarados alone. The legible target is the Chūgoku/Shikoku regional participation prize: Gyarados + Hiroshima route + Itsukushima Shrine floating torii context.
steps: Confirm the card is a Japanese World Challenge Summer Lucky Stadium regional print, not the English Neo Destiny 100/105 card.
Confirm the featured Pokemon is Gyarados; other regional World Challenge Summer prints feature Onix, Lugia, Ho-Oh, Zapdos, Diglett, Mew, or Pikachu.
Ask for clear front images of the regional artwork and any readable event/region text; Chūgoku/Shikoku should not be inferred from Lucky Stadium name alone.
Treat marketplace shorthand such as 'Chugoku Lucky Stadium' as a search clue, not a full identity; compare it against Bulbapedia's Chūgoku/Shikoku region naming.

Screen against the Tropical Mega Battle bilingual Lucky Stadium, Intro Pack Neo Lucky Stadium, Pokemon Center New York Lucky Stadium, ordinary Neo Destiny Lucky Stadium, and later Stadium cards before publishing a confident row match.
Do not promote regional identity into authenticity, possession, condition, or price truth.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors row 169 as Lucky Stadium in the World Challenge Summer Chūgoku/Shikoku participation-prize source group, with Gyarados as the row's distinguishing Pokemon signal.
Bulbapedia identifies Lucky Stadium as a Stadium card and lists the Japanese name as ラッキースタジアム Lucky Stadium.
Bulbapedia's card text for the Neo Destiny-style Lucky Stadium effect lets each player flip a coin once during their turn before attacking; on heads, that player draws a card.
Bulbapedia and PokeBoon both associate the Chūgoku/Shikoku Gyarados Lucky Stadium artwork with Yousuke Hirata and CR CG gangs.

As judged art texture, the Chūgoku/Shikoku card works because Gyarados and the floating torii both imply passage through water, making the regional landmark feel almost mythic inside a tournament prize.

The Chūgoku/Shikoku print is one member of an eight-print World Challenge Summer regional set; Bulbapedia lists separate region/Pokemon pairings for Kyūshū/Onix, Kantō/Lugia, Kansai/Ho-Oh, Hokkaidō/Pikachu, Chūbu/Zapdos, Hokushin'etsu/Mew, and Tōhoku/Diglett.

As judged collector texture, Lucky Stadium [Gyarados] [Chūgoku/Shikoku] rewards exactness: Gyarados, Itsukushima, Hiroshima, and the shared Stadium effect all have to stay distinct from the other seven regional prints.

narrative.human_title: Lucky Stadium [Gyarados] [Chūgoku/Shikoku]: water at the gate
narrative.why_it_matters: This is one of the regional Stadiums where the pairing feels almost too perfect. Gyarados is motion and menace; Itsukushima's torii is a gate standing in water. Put them inside a tournament participation card from Hiroshima and the result is no longer generic Lucky Stadium. It is a small regional myth, indexed by cardboard.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A card-level Lucky Stadium match is being prepared for a want, sale, dossier, or agent comparison.
special_identification_instructions.summary: The card name is too broad. Confirm the Chūgoku/Shikoku regional print by Gyarados, torii/event cues, and exclusion of the other Lucky Stadium routes.
steps: Confirm the front artwork features Gyarados; this is the Chūgoku/Shikoku print's key Pokemon cue.
Ask for close images of any region/event text and the whole artwork field; do not infer Chūgoku/Shikoku from a seller title alone.
Compare against all other World Challenge Summer regional prints: Onix, Lugia, Ho-Oh, Zapdos, Diglett, Mew, and Pikachu variants.
Compare against the Tropical Mega Battle bilingual Lucky Stadium and ordinary Neo Destiny / Intro Pack Neo / New York City Lucky Stadium prints.
Treat 'Chugoku' marketplace shorthand as useful but incomplete; the source row is Chūgoku/Shikoku and needs artwork/route support.
Do not treat CGC/PSA population, auction title, or marketplace category as physical-card proof without matching images and seller evidence.
